items.title: Water Minute · Why your skin feels tight after a shower
items.preview:
Words I like;
Clean water isn't a luxury. It's the baseline your body was built for.
Ever notice how your skin feels tight and itchy right after a shower, like you need lotion before the towel even hits the floor? That's not your soap. That's hard water.
Here's what's actually happening. Hard water is loaded with calcium and magnesium. When those minerals hit your soap, they don't rinse clean. They bind together and leave a film, kind of like the ring you see around a bathtub. Except now that film is sitting on your skin.
That film clogs pores, strips the natural oils your skin uses to stay soft, and throws off your skin's protective barrier. For folks with eczema or sensitive skin, it makes flare-ups worse. Kids feel it fastest, because their skin is thinner.
Soft water rinses clean. No film, no residue. Your natural oils stay put, and your skin does what it's supposed to do on its own.
If you already softened your water, that itchy tight feeling you used to fight every winter? That's the problem you paid to solve, and it stayed solved.
Curious what's really in your water? Reply and I'll send you our free water assessment.
As promised, value in under a minute.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave

items.title: Email Campaign · : Year-1.5 Concierge "Is it worth it?" (highest conversion)
items.preview:
**Audience:** Concierge upsell candidates, 100 members (13 to 24 months post-install, already had year-1 service, not on Concierge). Compliant with the 12-month floor.
**Why this one:** These people already trusted us with a paid annual service, so the relationship is warm and the ask is low-friction. Highest revenue-per-open of any segment this week ($99/mo recurring).
### Subject line (+ alternates)
- **Primary (specific):** The year 1.5 question we get asked most
- **Curiosity:** Is Concierge actually worth it for you?
- **Pain:** Tired of remembering filter swaps?
- **Authority:** Here is the honest Concierge math
- **Specific:** $99/mo: what it does and does not cover
### Preview text
Not a pitch. Just the math, so you can decide for yourself.
### Body
Hi [First Name],
It's been about [X months] since we installed your water system, which means you're past your first annual service. So you now know how we operate.
There's one question we get a lot right around this point: "Is this Concierge thing actually worth it for me?"
Fair question. Here's the honest math, no spin.
Concierge is $99/mo and covers:
- Your annual service (the one you already pay for)
- Filter swaps
- Priority phone support
- Parts coverage on your standard install components
If you'd rather stay pay-as-you-go, that's completely fine. Plenty of our clients do, and your system is built to run clean with very little fuss either way. This is just so you have the numbers in front of you instead of wondering.
Want me to run your specific setup and tell you whether it pencils out? Just reply "math" and I'll send it over.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
*(Note: for the two Albert Romano duplicate records, dedupe to one send. Records with a current ClearWave name in the system field are absent here, so all use the tenure line.)*
### Send timing
**Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET.** Mid-morning Tuesday is the strongest B2C open window for an existing-customer audience, and small volume protects reputation.
### Expected performance
- **Open: 35 to 45%.** Warm audience + curiosity subject with zero spam-trigger words. Should approach the 42.3% historical average (the recent 0.4% opens were content/deliverability driven, not audience).
- **Click/reply: 6 to 10%.** "Reply math" is a single low-friction CTA.
- **Conversion: 4 to 8 sign-ups** (~$400 to $800/mo recurring = $4.8k to $9.6k annualized) at even a modest close on 100 warm contacts.
### Source justification
Draws from **Jobber conciergeUpsellCandidates trigger** (already filtered to 13 to 24 months, pre-cleared against the 12-month hard floor) and the **Concierge Upsell Context** block ("the question we get asked at year 1.5... here's the math," non-pushy framing, exact $99/mo inclusions).

items.title: Email Campaign · : 30-to-60-Day Referral Push (warm, high-intent)
items.preview:
**Audience:** Referral push candidates, 30 members (30 to 60 days post-install, satisfied). Well past the year-1 restriction on service pitches, and referrals are always allowed (Rule #3).
**Why this one:** Fresh installs = peak enthusiasm. This is the ideal window to convert goodwill into referrals, and it pushes referrals/testimonials (compliant) rather than reviews.
### Subject line (+ alternates)
- **Primary (specific):** $500 for the first person you send our way
- **Curiosity:** Who else in [City] has water like yours?
- **Authority:** Our clients are our whole growth engine
- **Pain:** Know someone stuck with bad water?
- **Specific:** How the ClearWave referral bonus works
### Preview text
Real cash, real numbers, and it stacks the more you send.
### Body
Hi [First Name],
You've had your ClearWave system for a little over a month now, so the water's had time to speak for itself.
Here's the thing: we don't spend much on ads. We grow because people like you tell a neighbor. So we make it worth your while.
If you refer someone and they become a client:
- $500 cash for each of your first five this year
- $750 for six through nine
- $1,000 each once you hit ten (it resets every January)
And if someone you send books a consult but doesn't move forward, you still get a $50 gift card just for the intro.
All they need is a free water assessment. That's the one next step. Send me their name and the best number, or forward this straight to them.
Know someone in [City] fighting hard water or funky well water? I'd love to help them the way we helped you.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
*(For clients whose system field is a current ClearWave name (e.g. Chris Miller: "Meridian + RO," Janine Stenson: "ClearWave Sovereign"), you may name it. All others use "your ClearWave system" or the tenure line. Regina Ryan / Stacy Durfee = tenure line, legacy/unspecified.)*
### Send timing
**Thursday, 11:00 AM ET.** Spacing it two days after the Concierge send avoids fatiguing the shared audience and keeps daily send volume low for reputation repair.
### Expected performance
- **Open: 38 to 48%.** Very warm (30 to 60 days in), the specific "$500" subject drives curiosity without a discount trigger.
- **Click/reply: 5 to 9%.** Two easy CTAs (reply a name or forward).
- **Conversion: 2 to 5 warm referral intros.** Even one closed referral returns $500+ in pipeline; forwarding lifts reach beyond the 30.
### Source justification
Draws from the **Jobber referralPushCandidates trigger** (30 to 60 days post-install, satisfied) and the **Referral Bonus Structure** block (exact $500/$750/$1,000 tiers, $50 gift card, "free water assessment" phrasing per Rule 3a), while respecting Rule #3 (referrals not reviews).
---
## What I deliberately did NOT propose this week
- **Cold lead re-engagement (1,000):** Highest-volume opportunity, but sending 1,000 to a cold, unengaged list right now would deepen the deliverability hole. Warm up with the two small sends above first, then I'll bring you a news-angle re-engagement next week.
- **1-year annual service candidates (15):** These are service reminders, not a campaign with strong conversion economics, and several (Winslow, total $0) look incomplete. Better handled by Jobber's transactional reminders.
- **RO replacement-cycle (27):** Viable next week, but lower priority than the recurring-revenue Concierge play.
Want me to prep the cold-lead re-engagement draft (water-news angle + free water assessment CTA) for next week once these two land?

---

*Generated by the Email Sub-Agent · idea sourcing per IDEA_SOURCING.md · sign-off rule: "Justin / CEO / ClearWave" two-line, no em dash prefix.*
